subject: Mathematics
unit: Summer 1: Geometric notation and constructions; geometric reasoning
source: Seeded from mathematics/y7 lesson 61 (Printable construction sheet: perpendiculars (portal worksheet for this lesson))
intro: Lesson 61: Constructing perpendiculars and shortest distances. To understand how to construct perpendiculars from a point and at a point, and use them to find shortest distances

model.title: Construct the perpendicular from point P to line l.

parts.label: Step 1
parts.text: Arc from P cutting l at A and B

parts.label: Step 2
parts.text: Same radius: arcs from A and B on the other side of l

parts.label: Step 3
parts.text: Join P to the crossing point

model.title: Construct a right angle at point Q on a line.

parts.label: Step 1
parts.text: Arcs from Q cut the line at A and B, so QA = QB

parts.label: Step 2
parts.text: Wider radius: arcs from A and B crossing above Q

questions.q: Draw a line and a point P 5 cm above it. Construct the perpendicular from P and measure the shortest distance.
questions.model: Arc from P cutting the line twice. Equal arcs from those points below the line; join P to the crossing. Measure from P to the foot: 5 cm.

questions.q: Construct a right angle at the 3 cm mark of a 10 cm line.
questions.a: Perpendicular at a point on the line

questions.q: Why is the height of a triangle measured along a perpendicular?
questions.a: Height is the shortest distance from the vertex to the base, which is along the perpendicular.

questions.q: (a) Construct a square of side 5 cm using perpendiculars (no protractor). (b) Draw triangle ABC with AB = 8 cm, AC = 6 cm, BC = 7 cm and construct the perpendicular from C to AB. Measure the height. (c) Work out the area: ½ × 8 × height.
questions.a: (a) right angles at the corners, sides 5 cm (b) height ≈ 5.1 cm (c) area ≈ 20.3 cm² (accept 20 to 21 cm²)
questions.model: (a) Draw 5 cm. Construct a perpendicular at each end. Measure 5 cm up each one and join the tops.

questions.q: A ship S is 6 km from a straight coastline (scale 1 cm = 1 km). Construct the point on the coast closest to the ship.
questions.a: The foot of the perpendicular from S to the coastline, 6 cm from S on the drawing.

questions.q: Explain why the perpendicular from the top of an isosceles triangle cuts the base in half.
questions.a: It makes two right-angled triangles with equal hypotenuses and a shared side, so by Pythagoras their bases are equal.

questions.q: The shortest distance from a point to a line is:
What angle does a constructed perpendicular make with the line?
Big question: what is the shortest path from a point to a straight road?
questions.a: The perpendicular: the path that meets the road at 90°.
